paper_metadata.title: A Threshold for Quantum Advantage in Derivative Pricing

summary: This paper provides end-to-end fault-tolerant resource estimates for gate-based quantum derivative pricing, focusing on a basket autocallable and a TARF under geometric Brownian motion. Using the re-parameterization method with IQAE, it estimates about 8k logical qubits and T-depth 5.4e7 for the autocallable, and 11.5k logical qubits with T-depth 8.2e7 for the TARF; the older Riemann-summation approach is worse, at roughly 23k qubits/1.5e8 T-depth for the autocallable and 17k qubits/1.6e8 T-depth for the TARF.

experiments.description: End-to-end gate-based quantum derivative pricing for a basket autocallable option using the re-parameterization method with variationally trained Gaussian loaders and amplitude estimation.

algorithm.variant: Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (IQAE) with re-parameterization path loading
algorithm.ansatz: Ry-CNOT ansatz for Gaussian state preparation
algorithm.optimizer: BFGS after COBYLA warm-up for variational Gaussian-loader training
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Warm-start from previous optimization depth; continuous parameters projected to nearest digitized grid point for fault-tolerant discussion

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Paths are loaded as a superposition over dT Gaussian-distributed log-return registers; payoffs are normalized and rotated into an ancilla amplitude
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate expected discounted payoff E(f) via amplitude estimation after loading path distribution and payoff into ancilla amplitude
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Normalization of payoff to [0,1]; no QUBO/Ising formulation

problem_instance.description: Basket autocallable with 5 autocall dates and a knock-in put, priced under geometric Brownian motion

dataset_specification.description: Geometric Brownian motion model; no market dataset used

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Modeling in return space; log-returns discretized in window [-w*sigma_max, w*sigma_max]; cumulative returns used for payoff logic
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Resource estimate for target error 2e-3; confidence level 68%; no empirical benchmark runs reported

implementation_details.classical_solver: Monte Carlo (classical baseline for comparison only)
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical calibration of Gaussian-loader parameters; Cholesky decomposition of covariance matrix; digitization of variational angles discussed
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescale normalized expected payoff back to original units
implementation_details.quantum_execution_time: ~1 second target discussed in discussion section

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Gaussian-loader training error decreases approximately exponentially with depth in numerical study

speedup_claims.conditions: using amplitude estimation; fault-tolerant setting; target error 2e-3
speedup_claims.caveats: End-to-end advantage depends on large fault-tolerant overheads; paper emphasizes resource requirements are out of reach of current systems.

speedup_claims.conditions: assuming T-gates at 10 MHz and sufficient code distance for 10^10 logical operations
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a projected threshold, not an executed hardware result.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) oracle calls for amplitude estimation; end-to-end resource estimate dominated by T-depth and fault-tolerant arithmetic
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(M)) Monte Carlo convergence for M sampled paths
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: T-depth about 5.4e7 for the autocallable benchmark
complexity_analysis.total_operations_classical: Classical Monte Carlo requires at least 40000 paths for the cited practical pricing context; asymptotic error O(M^-1/2)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 5-10 seconds using classical Monte Carlo for similar products, as stated in background

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; paper gives only resource estimates, not a crossover point
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: About 8k logical qubits and T-depth 5.4e7 for the basket autocallable benchmark; target runtime discussed is ~1 second
limiting_factors: Quadratic speedup from amplitude estimation is offset by error-correction overhead

notes: circuit_depth is not given as a single depth for the full end-to-end algorithm; the paper reports T-depth = 5.4e7 for the autocallable benchmark, which is used here as the main depth resource metric
hardware not specified because the paper is a resource-estimation study rather than an executed hardware experiment
The paper reports a resource estimate, not an experimental advantage demonstration.
The authors explicitly state current systems are out of reach.

experiments.description: Variational Gaussian-loader training study for preparing standard normal states using an Ry-CNOT ansatz, evaluated by L∞ error versus circuit depth and register size.

algorithm.variant: Variational Gaussian loader training; energy-based pretraining followed by L∞ re-optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Best of 8 independent optimization runs per configuration; no explicit stopping threshold reported
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Start from previous depth solution when available; for digitized study, project continuous parameters to nearest grid point and locally search

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare discretized standard normal distribution on n qubits over xi=-w+iΔx
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize L∞ distance between prepared distribution and target discretized Gaussian; energy of quantum harmonic oscillator used as pretraining objective
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Quantum harmonic oscillator H = P^2/(2m) + m(X-x0)^2/2

problem_instance.description: Standard normal distribution loading subproblem used to support the re-parameterization method

dataset_specification.description: Discretized Gaussian on a finite interval [-w,w]

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Target distribution normalized as g(xi)Δx over 2^n bins; energy-based training uses harmonic-oscillator ground state; then L∞ refinement and digitization to finite angle grid
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Eight independent optimization runs for each (n,L); best run reported; error curves shown versus depth and digitization mesh size

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical optimization loop with COBYLA then BFGS; parameter digitization and local search on grid
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute L∞ norm between prepared and target distributions; compare energy and L∞ landscapes

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: L∞ error decreases approximately exponentially with depth; direct L∞ optimization often trapped in poor local minima

speedup_claims.conditions: fault-tolerant implementation of single-qubit rotations; approximation accuracy epsilon
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity statement about gate synthesis and approximation, not a demonstrated end-to-end speedup for pricing.
The study supports a subroutine for the main pricing algorithms; it does not itself establish quantum advantage.
